title: A visit to the school garden
text: Hi, Lucy. It's Emma. Here is some news about our school garden visit. We're going on Friday, not Thursday, because our teacher has a meeting on Thursday. Please meet us outside the library at half past nine. We won't need the school bus. The garden is only ten minutes away, so we'll walk there. You should bring a small notebook and a pencil. The gardeners will give us gloves. First, we'll look at the vegetables. Then we'll plant some flowers in pairs. We'll have lunch back at school. I'm really looking forward to working outside with you!

title: A surprise for Grandma
text: Hello, Mia. It's Sophie. Can you help me with Grandma's birthday on Sunday? She thinks we're taking her to a restaurant, but we're making lunch at our house instead. Dad is cooking vegetable soup, and I'm making a chocolate cake. Grandma loves chocolate, but she doesn't like coffee, so please don't bring a coffee cake. My brother will decorate the sitting room with paper flowers. Could you arrive at eleven? Grandma is coming at twelve. We want to finish everything before she gets here. You don't need to buy a present. Please bring the old family photographs we looked at last week.

title: The swimming club
text: Hi, Anna. It's Grace. I tried the new swimming club yesterday, and I think you'll like it. The lessons are on Wednesdays after school. I usually cycle to the pool, but yesterday Mum drove me because it was raining. Our coach is called Mrs Bell. She is very friendly and explains everything slowly. There are eight children in my group. We practised moving our arms and then played a game in the water. I forgot my towel, but the coach found a clean one for me. Next week, I'll pack my bag the night before. Would you like to come with me?

title: A lost scarf
text: Hello, Kate. It's Lily. I think I left my scarf at your house after our film night. It's green with little white stars. I took it off in the kitchen when we made sandwiches, but then I carried it into the sitting room. Could you look behind the sofa? I was sitting there with your cat. Please don't bring it to school tomorrow because I'm staying at home with a cold. My dad can collect it from your house on his way back from work. He'll arrive at about six. Thanks for helping me. I really enjoyed the film, especially the funny dog!

title: The class play
text: Hi, Ruby. It's Alice. Our teacher has changed the time of the class play. It will start at four o'clock on Tuesday, an hour earlier than we planned. We must be in the hall at three to get ready. I'm playing a shopkeeper, and you're a customer. Please wear your blue jacket, not your red one. The blue one looks better with the hat Mrs Green found. You don't need to learn any new words. We're using the same short conversation we practised yesterday. After the play, our parents can have tea in the classroom. My mum is bringing biscuits for everyone.

title: A weekend bike ride
text: Hello, Ellie. It's Charlotte. Our family is going for a bike ride on Saturday. Would you like to join us? We'll follow the path beside the river. It is flat, so it won't be a difficult ride. My little sister is coming too. We wanted to leave at nine, but the bike shop doesn't open until ten. Dad needs to collect his bike there first. Let's meet at our gate at half past ten. We'll stop for a picnic near the old bridge. Please bring a bottle of water. Mum is making enough sandwiches for everyone, and Dad has checked the weather. It should be dry.

title: Looking after a rabbit
text: Hi, Olivia. It's Hannah. Thank you for looking after my rabbit while we're away. His name is Snowy, but he isn't white. He's grey with a small white nose. Please give him fresh water every morning. There is rabbit food in the green box beside his cage. He can have a little carrot as well, but not a whole one every day. He likes sitting quietly near people. Please keep the garden gate closed when he is outside. We leave on Monday and come home on Friday evening. I'll call you on Wednesday to hear how he is. Thanks again for your help.

title: Books for the fair
text: Hello, Zoe. It's Isabel. The school book fair is next week, and our class is collecting books for younger children. Please choose books that are clean and have all their pages. They don't have to be new. I found three animal stories and a book of simple poems at home. We should take our books to Room Twelve by Thursday morning. The fair opens on Friday afternoon. Our class won't sell food this time, but the music club will play in the hall. I'd like to help on the book table after lunch. Can you help too? Mrs Hill says we can work together.

title: A change of picnic plans
text: Hi, Ella. It's Freya. We need to change our picnic plans because of the weather. The forecast says it will rain heavily on Sunday, so we're meeting on Saturday instead. We won't go to the beach. The little park near my house has a covered table where we can sit if it rains a little. Let's meet there at one o'clock. I've made some fruit salad, and my brother is bringing cheese sandwiches. Could you bring a board game? We can play it after lunch. Please leave your football at home because there isn't much space around the table. Call me when you hear this message.

title: The art competition
text: Hello, Eva. It's Poppy. I have some information about the school art competition. This year's subject is our town in winter. Last year we painted summer gardens, so please don't use your old picture. You can use pencils or paint, but not photographs. The picture must be smaller than the classroom noticeboard, of course! Write your name and class on the back. Give your work to Mr Brown by Monday. He'll put all the pictures in the library on Wednesday. The winner will receive a set of paints, not money. I'm drawing the market square with snow on the roofs. What are you going to draw?

title: The science museum trip
text: Hi, Millie. It's Daisy. I've just read the letter about our museum trip. We need to be at school at eight fifteen, because the bus leaves at half past eight. Please bring a packed lunch. There is a cafe at the museum, but our class won't eat there. In the morning, we'll visit the room about space. After lunch, a guide will show us how a simple bridge works. You can take photographs in most rooms, but not during the bridge talk. We'll return at four. My dad can take you home with me if your parents are busy. Let me know tonight.

title: Making breakfast
text: Hello, Rose. It's Amelie. We're making breakfast for Dad tomorrow because it's his birthday. Mum will keep him busy in the garden while we cook. My brother wanted to make eggs, but Dad prefers porridge with fruit. I'll make the porridge, and you can cut the bananas. There are apples too, but please save them for Mum's cake. Dad usually drinks tea with breakfast, so we don't need to make coffee. Please come at eight. We want everything ready at half past eight, before Dad comes inside. You can borrow my apron. Don't worry about washing the dishes afterwards; my brother has promised to do that.

title: Joining the music group
text: Hi, Bella. It's Florence. I went to the school music group this afternoon. You don't have to play an instrument to join. Some children sing, and others help with the sound. I took my guitar, but the teacher asked me to sing a short song first. The group meets on Mondays in the small music room, not in the hall. Our first concert is in December. We're going to practise two cheerful songs for it. There are no meetings during the school holidays. If you want to join, speak to Miss White before Friday. She'll give you a form to take home to your parents.

title: The new neighbour
text: Hello, Clara. It's Matilda. A new family has moved into the flat above ours. Their daughter is called Nina, and she's eleven, just like us. She speaks English and Spanish. She hasn't started at our school yet; her first day is next Monday. Nina loves making things from paper, but she doesn't enjoy computer games very much. I invited her to our craft afternoon on Saturday. Could you bring your coloured paper? I have scissors and glue. We'll meet at my flat at two. Nina has a little dog, but her parents will look after him while we're busy. I think you'll like her.

title: Helping at the sports day
text: Hi, Esme. It's Beatrice. Mrs Fox needs two helpers for the younger children's sports day. I said we could help with the beanbag game if you're free. The sports day is on Thursday morning, from ten until twelve. We won't miss Maths because our class has a free project morning then. Please wear trainers and your yellow school shirt so the children can find us easily. We need to count the beanbags and explain the game. We don't have to choose the winners; a teacher will do that. Afterwards, the helpers can have juice and fruit in the hall. Can you tell me tomorrow if you're coming?

title: The holiday postcard
text: Hello, Nora. It's Harriet. We're having a lovely holiday by the lake. I sent you a postcard yesterday, but it may arrive after we get home! We're staying in a small wooden house with my aunt and uncle. The mornings are cool, so I wear a jumper when we go for walks. In the afternoon, it's warm enough to sit outside. Yesterday, we hired a boat. Uncle Ben rowed while I took photographs of the birds. I didn't swim because the water was cold. Tomorrow, we're visiting a village market. I'd like to buy a little notebook there. We'll be home on Sunday evening.

title: The class newspaper
text: Hi, Molly. It's Imogen. Our first class newspaper is nearly ready. It will have six pages, including the front page. I've written a story about our school cat, and Jack has drawn a map of the playground. We still need someone to write about the football match. Could you do that? Please keep it short, about sixty words. Send your story to our teacher by Tuesday evening. We will check everything on Wednesday and print the newspaper on Friday. It won't cost anything; each pupil will get one copy. The library will have two extra copies for visitors. Thanks for helping us finish it.

title: A visit to the farm
text: Hello, Ada. It's Eliza. The farm has sent us the programme for Saturday. We should arrive at ten, but the animal talk doesn't start until half past ten. Please wear old clothes and boots. The paths may be muddy after the rain. We'll watch the farmer feed the goats, but we mustn't give them our own food. After the talk, we can help collect eggs. My cousin is coming with us, but my little brother will stay at home. We'll bring our own lunch and eat it at the picnic tables. There is a shop, but you don't need money unless you want a souvenir.

title: The reading challenge
text: Hi, Leah. It's Phoebe. I've joined the library reading challenge, and you can still join too. We have to read four books before the end of August. They can be stories, poems or information books, but magazines don't count. After each book, we tell the librarian one thing we liked about it. We don't have to write a long report. I've already finished a story about a lost puppy. Next, I'm choosing a book about space. When we finish all four books, we get a certificate and a bookmark. The library is closed on Mondays, so shall we go together on Tuesday afternoon?

title: A walk with a camera
text: Hello, Maisie. It's Evelyn. The photography club is going for a walk on Sunday. We will meet at the old clock in the town square at eleven. Our teacher wants us to photograph doors and windows, not people. You can use a simple camera or your phone. Please make sure the battery is charged. The walk will take about an hour. Afterwards, we'll choose our favourite photographs in the library. There isn't a competition, so nobody will get a prize. We're just learning to notice interesting shapes and colours. If it rains, we'll stay inside the library and photograph objects there instead. I hope you can come.
